title: Logistics/Mobility Chief (MGySgt to GySgt) PMOS, DC I&L
raw_text:
10.     MOS 0491, Logistics/Mobility Chief (MGySgt to GySgt) PMOS, DC I&L

    a. Summary. The Logistics/Mobility Chief coordinates, plans, conducts,
and supervises logistics operations throughout various levels of the Marine


                                            3-52                        Enclosure (1)
 3111                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



Corps. They serve on general officer staffs at the MEF, MARFOR, and HQMC
level where they conduct planning and execution of MAGTF deployments from the
tactical to strategic level. Additionally, Logistics/Mobility Chiefs
articulate logistical and strategic mobility requirements to appropriate
agencies both inside and outside the Service. Furthermore, assignments to
embed within the U.S. Navy as combat cargo assistants (CCAs) aboard naval
amphibious warfare ships and within various commands of the Navy. Lastly,
Logistics/Mobility Chiefs facilitate unit level logistics and embarkation
training within their commands.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must have had previous duty as an 0441 or a 0471 USMCR.

        (2) Logistics/Mobility follow-on courses that enhance MOS proficiency
are identified in the current version of the MOS Roadmap within the Marine
Corps Training Information Management System (MCTIMS). Listed courses
outline which course directly contribute to the growth of the 0491.

        (3) The completion of listed courses enhances proficiency and
increases the probability of Marines being promoted to the next grade.
Marines who complete all identified courses will be viewed has highly
competitive for promotion and set themselves apart from their peers.

        (4) These courses and their completion coincide with requirements
identified within the most current version on the Logistics Training and
Readiness Manual which contribute to the professional capability of the
individual Marine and capacity within the logistics community.

    c. Requirements. Upon promotion to the rank of Gunnery Sergeant, the
MOS 0491 will be granted and reported in MCTFS.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (f), Logistics Training and Readiness Manual.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
First-Line Supervisors/Managers of Officer and Administrative Support Workers
43-1011.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.




                                          3-53                       Enclosure (1)
 3112                                                              NAVMC 1200.1L

Logistics is the science of planning and carrying out the movement and maintenance of forces. It includes the design, development, acquisition, storage, movement, distribution, maintenance, evacuation, and disposition of material, the movement, evacuation, and hospitalization of personnel, the acquisition or construction, maintenance, operation, and disposition of facilities, and the acquisition or furnishings of services. Logistics functions are performed by a wide variety of MOSs in various occupational fields. Enlisted specialties within occupational field 04 provide advice, guidance, logistics/combat service support, embarkation, landing support, and air delivery.

Furthermore, assignments to embed within the U.S. Navy as combat cargo assistants (CCAs) aboard naval amphibious warfare ships and within various commands of the Navy. Lastly, Logistics/Mobility Chiefs facilitate unit level logistics and embarkation training within their commands. b. Prerequisites (1) Must have had previous duty as an 0441 or a 0471 USMCR. (2) Logistics/Mobility follow-on courses that enhance MOS proficiency are identified in the current version of the MOS Roadmap within the Marine Corps Training Information Management System (MCTIMS). Listed courses outline which course directly contribute to the growth of the 0491. (3) The completion of listed courses enhances proficiency and increases the probability of Marines being promoted to the next grade. Marines who complete all identified courses will be viewed has highly competitive for promotion and set themselves apart from their peers. (4) These courses and their completion coincide with requirements identified within the most current version on the Logistics Training and Readiness Manual which contribute to the professional capability of the individual Marine and capacity within the logistics community. c. Requirements. Upon promotion to the rank of Gunnery Sergeant, the MOS 0491 will be granted and reported in MCTFS. d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (f), Logistics Training and Readiness Manual.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
